result.title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
result.summary: Autonomous software agents can act through tools, delegate work, and change their models or execution environments while earlier authorizations remain in flight. We present Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA), an approach designed to be harness-independent, for maintaining operational authority according to currently justified assurance. It distinguishes evidence validity from contextual applicability, derives assurance claims from eligible evidence, and resolves a multidimensional effective-authority envelope within a principal-declared ceiling and applicable policy. A typed dependency graph supports selective re-evaluation of authorization-relevant changes. An authority epoch changes when effective authority changes; a distinct optional authorization-basis version supports revalidation of action-specific authorization conditions. Protected effect-time enforcement can reject stale actions before a consequential resource change, subject to the available commit mechanism. A compositional Domain Governance Profile expresses domain-specific semantics without granting authority. Controlled scenario tests implemented as a regression suite using a trading profile exercise default-deny rules, evidence-conditioned contraction and recovery, policy divergence, selective non-response, and stale-action rejection at a local gateway before the simulated-broker boundary. The study establishes implementation-level evidence in one domain, not a cross-domain guarantee of harmful-behavior prevention.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ACCA：一种与框架无关的自主 agent 持续授权机制，区分证据有效性与上下文适用性，借助有类型依赖图对授权相关变化做选择性重评估，用 authority epoch 标记有效权限变化，并在效果时刻拒绝陈旧动作，仅在交易域回归套件中做了实现级验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 「证据有效但上下文已不适用」以及按依赖结构选择性重评估、在动作生效前拒绝陈旧依据的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据何时失效、何时需重新看与停止决策的判据；但原文属 agent 授权治理，未涉及视觉或多模态推理，迁移仅为概念类比。
